However, it only throws NullPointerException when the static boolean flag ExoPlayerLibraryInfo.ASSERTIONS_ENABLED is true and the reference is null. If the flag is false, the method returns the reference even if it is null, effectively bypassing the null check. This pattern is typical for assertions that are enabled only during development or debugging. The throw statement is guarded by a condition that makes it a development-time check, not a runtime validation that always occurs. The method includes annotations like @EnsuresNonNull and a precondition that documents the throw, indicating that the exception is intended to signal a programming error when a null reference is passed. The execution flow thus conditionally throws the exception only in assertion-enabled environments.
